newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-ACOSTA SCORES FOUR GOALS IN LIBERTADORES CUP GAME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ACOSTA SCORES FOUR GOALS IN LIBERTADORES CUP GAME.

text.p: Argentine striker Alberto Acosta scored all four goals as Chile's Universidad Catolica beat Oriente Petrolero of Bolivia 4-0 in a South American Libertadores Cup tie on Tuesday.
The stocky forward began his single-handed demolition of the Bolivians when he blasted his team ahead in the 11th minute.
He then scored with headers in the 70th and 78th minutes and completed his tally two minutes from the end with a solo effort which saw him dribbling past a defender before shooting home.

In two second-leg matches played on Tuesday, Gremio of Brazil and five-times champions Penarol from Uruguay went through to the quarter-finals and left Paraguay and Colombia without any teams in the competition.
Gremio, champions in 1983 and 1995, scraped through against little-known Paraguayans Guarany after a penalty shoot-out in which only three of the 10 attempts were converted.

The hard-tackling Brazilians, who seem incapable of getting through a Libertadores game with all their players on the field, had defender Luciano dismissed in the 25th minute for a second bookable offence.
Luciano had come in for Paraguayan international Catalino Rivarola, suspended after being sent off in the first leg which Guarany won 2-1.

Hugo Oceval appeared to have given Guarany an unlikely win when he scored in the 85th minute to wipe out Paulo Nunes's earlier effort for Gremio but Rodrigo Gral struck for Gremio a minute later to level the aggregate score.
Colombia, who have been represented in the last two finals, were left without a team after Millonarios lost 3-2 on penalties to Penarol in Montevideo.

Penarol, who last won the title in 1987, cancelled out the Colombians' 2-0 first-leg win with a 3-1 victory in a bad-tempered game. With no extra-time or away goals rule used to settle ties, the match then went to penalties.
